## Bug report
Select doesn't work as expected inside Dialog element

### Current Behavior
![image](https://github.com/radix-ui/primitives/assets/105656186/6f45410f-adcd-4dcc-bf3b-6155fb8f8d94)

- When I try to close the select via `escape` doesn't work it closes the modal and the select overlay persists so you cannot click UI element only keyboard navigate
- Arrow keys ⇵  on select for navigation won't work inside dialog
- Select item selection and hover selection also won't work
- Dialog open and closes and then opens this happens instantly (it doesn't fully close and reopen). I checked this multiple times if I remove select from dialog it works perfectly

### Expected behavior

<!-- A clear and concise description of what you expected to happen. -->

- expected `escape` will close the select and the second `escape` will close the modal
- expected other events also work like navigation with arrow keys
- expected at least both overlays of dialog and select disappear on `escape` 

### Your environment

I also am experiencing this when I open a `Dialog` from an option in a `DropdownMenu`. It occurs within handlers that say they are to refocus when it gets programmatically defocused. Perhaps the other component tries to steal focus and then they have a war?

Edit: Also, as a hacky workaround I can trigger the callback that opens the drawer with a delay like `setTimeout(() => openDialog(), 100)`.

This is happening because the versions of `@radix-ui/react-focus-scope` don't match. In the sandbox provided, if you change `@radix-ui/react-dialog` to `1.0.3` and `@radix-ui/react-dropdown-menu` to `2.0.4` it will work as those versions have the same version of `@radix-ui/react-focus-scope`.

So either you need to install versions of packages with the same `@radix-ui/react-focus-scope` or force the same version via yarn resolutions or npm overrides.

  }

comments.body: @ling1726 WDYT about this?

Apparently there's a conflict of interest between tabster navigation and menu event handler.

By simply modifying this line of code https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui/blob/d755a63d9e2f7c46c1f0f7d96fa4b8ad8e8edc40/packages/react-components/react-toolbar/src/components/Toolbar/useToolbar.ts#L21

to `axis: 'horizontal'`, we indicate to tabster to not listen on vertical navigation, which basically solves the problem.

The question is, would it be a regression if we stop supporting vertical navigation on `Toolbar`, @chpalac @ling1726? FYI, Also v0 [menu as toolbar example](https://fluentsite.z22.web.core.windows.net/0.66.2/components/menu/definition#usage-toolbar) doesn't support vertical navigation.


> ⚠️ The other solution would be to dig into `Menu` + `Toolbar` interactions to see how we can consume this event although tabster might be preventing it

@bsunderhus Initially the `axis` was defined based on the `vertical` prop. `axis: vertical ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'`. After one round of a11y ( not sure if was @adamsamec or @kolaps33 ) it was requested to have it behaving the same because screen readers couldn't know the toolbar direction. 

If we are going to have down arrow to open the menu in the horizontal I guess that will still be true for the vertical toolbar?

> @bsunderhus Initially the `axis` was defined based on the `vertical` prop. `axis: vertical ? 'vertical' : 'horizontal'`. After one round of a11y ( not sure if was @adamsamec or @kolaps33 ) it was requested to have it behaving the same because screen readers couldn't know the toolbar direction.
> 
> If we are going to have down arrow to open the menu in the horizontal I guess that will still be true for the vertical toolbar?

Yes, that will still be true for a vertical toolbar. Ok, I'll investigate a possible solution without requiring to opt-out of both axis navigation

> @bsunderhus @chpalac it would be worth revisitng the requirement for using both vertical and horizontal arrow keys, since the WAI guidance suggests to only use one axis

According to our investigations it seems like some screen readers (VoiceOver if I'm not mistaken) doesn't make a distinction in navigation direction for a toolbar, which kind of makes it harder to support only a single direction, according to @adamsamec the ideal would be to have both directions supported for this widget, @ling1726 .

> > @bsunderhus @chpalac it would be worth revisitng the requirement for using both vertical and horizontal arrow keys, since the WAI guidance suggests to only use one axis
> 
> According to our investigations it seems like some screen readers (VoiceOver if I'm not mistaken) doesn't make a distinction in navigation direction for a toolbar, which kind of makes it harder to support only a single direction, according to @adamsamec the ideal would be to have both directions supported for this widget, @ling1726 .

@bsunderhus in that case, I don't think we can ever use the down arrow to open the menu since it will definitely need to be used for keyboard navigation. The two requirements directly contradict each other 👀👀.

The current behaviour seems to be the way we're going with for now. I'll be closing this in favor of our current implementation: down key will remain as a navigational key instead of opening the menu provided by overflow items on a toolbar

### Search keywords

IconButton, details, summary

### Latest version

### Steps to reproduce

Steps:
1. [Open this link to live example](https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/9vx6h9)
2. Use a Button, IconButton or ButtonBase component="summary" inside an html details.
3. Bring keyboard Focus to the Button, IconButton or BaseButton.
4. Press the Space or Enter key to open the details element.
5. Nothing happens.


### Current behavior

When the summary IconButton has keyboard focus and is clicked using the Space or Enter key, the details element does not expand.

Clicking the IconButton with the mouse correctly expands the details element.

### Expected behavior

When the summary IconButton has keyboard focus and is clicked using the Space or Enter key, it should open to show the contents of the details.

### Context

Building a navigation menu where the top-level navigation items are details-summary elements. Some of these top-level elements are icon buttons.

[Might these lines be the cause?](https://github.com/mui/material-ui/blob/56b2648a1d4b6596914d1edb05cdbfe0938ed472/packages/mui-material/src/ButtonBase/ButtonBase.js#L206C1-L208C6)

comments.body: @mnajdova Any idea why the default functionality is prevented when Button is rendered in non `button` elements ? This is preventing the default behaviour of `summary` element.

I would recommend using a controlled state for the summary open state, e.g. https://codesandbox.io/p/devbox/mui-details-summary-iconbutton-bug-forked-swr2n7?workspaceId=ws_LCQafiBEJ7ynffHYRMAZL.

The buttons component can handle only button and link as interactive components, the additional logic is for corner cases where you want for some reason to render non interactive element, like div, where it makes sense to prevent the default behaviour. Now, the summary is another interactive element by default, I would even argue that rendering it as a button is not expected, but I understanding the use-case, as you namely want to use the styles of the button components. I would recommend using the workaround for it.

Thanks for the explanation!

One thing worth highlighting is that the HTML `<summary>` element is natively interactive and expected to toggle its parent `<details>` when activated via keyboard (Enter / Space), per the HTML spec and accessibility expectations.

When `ButtonBase` prevents default keyboard behavior for non-`button` / non-`a` components, rendering `component="summary"` unintentionally suppresses this native interaction, leading to a keyboard accessibility regression (mouse still works, keyboard does not).

I understand the reasoning behind restricting keyboard handling to known interactive elements, but would it be feasible to:
- treat `summary` as a known interactive element similar to `button` / `a`, or
- provide an opt-in escape hatch (e.g. a prop) to preserve native keyboard behavior when using inherently interactive elements like `summary`?

Happy to help with a test case or PR if this is something the team would consider.
